subject: english
question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Either Sam or Ishita have invited her for the Christmas party.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb "**have**" after "**Either Sam or Ishita**."
 
• When using** "either...or"** with singular subjects, the verb should also be **singular.**
 
• The correct phrase should be "**has invited her**," ensuring **subject-verb agreement.**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Either Sam or Ishita **has invited her** for the Christmas party."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.
 
• **Option 2: "Either Sam or Ishita"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "for the Christmas party."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
